title: Ask now, answer later: asynchronous jobs
summary: Enqueue an op as a real background job, then Poll its correlation value.
learning_objective: Enqueue asynchronous jobs, poll correlation values, and manage background tasks using KMIP asynchronous processing operations.

title: Certificate Services: a real X.509 CA, PQC included
summary: Certify / Re-certify / Validate — pure Rust, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA chains included.
learning_objective: Validate X.509 certificates using ECDSA and ML-DSA algorithms and detect tampering via Validity Indicators.

title: A new option: hash-based signatures
summary: SLH-DSA has no classical predecessor — a conservative addition, not a replacement.
learning_objective: Generate and verify signatures using SLH-DSA to implement a conservative, hash-based cryptographic hedge alongside lattice-based schemes.

title: An honest HSM: claims you can check
summary: Destroy really scrubs, read-only refuses, Locate really filters.
learning_objective: Verify HSM honesty by confirming read-only refusals, secure key destruction, and accurate Locate filtering.

title: Hedging your bets: hybrid key establishment
summary: X25519MLKEM768 — one op, two algorithms, secure if either survives.
learning_objective: Execute hybrid key encapsulation using X25519MLKEM768 to ensure security if either classical or post-quantum algorithms fail.

title: Key establishment
summary: ECDH → ML-KEM-768 — same goal, a completely different wire shape.
learning_objective: Implement ML-KEM-768 key establishment using KMIP Encapsulate and Decapsulate operations to replace classical ECDH workflows.

title: Provisioning a key
summary: CreateKeyPair → Activate — the object model everything else builds on.
learning_objective: Provision and activate RSA-3072 and ML-DSA-65 key pairs using KMIP CreateKeyPair and Activate operations.

title: Sign & verify
summary: RSA-3072 / ECDSA → ML-DSA-65 — the biggest visible size jump under PQC.
learning_objective: Compare RSA-3072 and ML-DSA-65 signature sizes to identify required buffer expansions for post-quantum migration.

title: Split custody: M-of-N key shares
summary: Split a key into 5 shares where any 3 recover it — and 2 honestly cannot.
learning_objective: Split a key into shares and reconstruct it using a threshold while verifying that fewer shares fail.

title: Myth-buster: AES-256 doesn't need to change
summary: The shortest lesson here, on purpose — the answer is "nothing changes."
learning_objective: Explain why AES-256 requires no changes for post-quantum security and prioritize migration budgets for asymmetric cryptography.

title: Capstone — from workbench to wire
summary: Every artifact so far has stayed inside the Workbench's virtual filesystem. This lesson generates one final certificate, then hands off to the Studio's TLS Simulator — a separate tool that runs a real TLS 1.3 handshake in WASM — to see a certificate actually used on the wire.
learning_objective: Execute a TLS 1.3 handshake using a generated ML-DSA certificate in the TLS Simulator.
reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 (content review vs openssl docs + bundled 3.6.3 binary)

title: Requesting and issuing a certificate
summary: req -new produces a CSR for a CA to sign; req -x509 -new skips straight to a self-signed certificate. Both classical and PQC keys go through the identical req command.
learning_objective: Self-sign classical and post-quantum certificates using identical OpenSSL req commands to demonstrate algorithm-agnostic certificate issuance workflows.
reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 (content review vs openssl docs + bundled 3.6.3 binary)

title: Config files demystified
summary: openssl.cnf quietly supplies defaults every req/x509 call in this curriculum relied on. openssl configutl (new in OpenSSL 3.6) parses and re-dumps a config file so you can see exactly what it resolves to.
learning_objective: Parse and linearize OpenSSL configuration files to inspect resolved defaults and stripped comments.
reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 (content review vs openssl docs + bundled 3.6.3 binary)

title: Your first keypair — classical, then post-quantum
summary: genpkey generates both eras of key with the same command shape — only the -algorithm value changes. Watch what changes (and what stays the same) between an RSA-2048 key and an ML-DSA-65 key.
learning_objective: Generate classical RSA and post-quantum ML-DSA private keys using OpenSSL's genpkey command.

title: An honest LMS — a claim you can check yourself
summary: This Studio's LMS/HSS panel generates and signs via a separate WASM engine, not openssl itself — because upstream OpenSSL genuinely does not support LMS/HSS key generation or signing. Don't take that on faith: break the rule yourself and read the real error.
learning_objective: Verify OpenSSL's refusal to generate LMS/HSS keys and explain the security rationale behind this design decision.

title: Key derivation, chosen correctly
summary: openssl kdf (new in OpenSSL 3.6) exposes HKDF, PBKDF2, SCRYPT and more behind one command. Each expects different -kdfopt keys — mixing them up is the most common way to get a useless key silently.
learning_objective: Select the correct KDF algorithm and input options to derive keys from secrets or passwords without silent security failures.
reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 (content review vs openssl docs + bundled 3.6.3 binary)

title: Key establishment without classical key exchange
summary: ML-KEM has no drop-in classical equivalent in this Studio — it's a genuinely new operation shape (encapsulate/decapsulate) rather than a PQC repaint of an existing one. This lesson runs the full round trip and checks the recovered secret really matches.
learning_objective: Execute ML-KEM encapsulation and decapsulation to generate and verify a shared secret without classical key exchange.

title: Packaging keys for the real world
summary: pkcs12 bundles a key + certificate (+ chain) into one password-protected file — the format most browsers and app servers actually import. Classical and PQC keys bundle identically.
learning_objective: Bundle cryptographic keys and certificates into a password-protected PKCS#12 file for deployment to browsers and application servers.
reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 (content review vs openssl docs + bundled 3.6.3 binary)

title: Randomness, honestly sourced
summary: Every key this Studio has generated so far leaned on openssl rand under the hood. This lesson calls it directly and looks at what it actually promises.
learning_objective: Invoke openssl rand to generate random bytes and verify its failure behavior on entropy seeding errors.
reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 (content review vs openssl docs + bundled 3.6.3 binary)

title: Sign & verify, two ways
summary: Classical keys sign through dgst (hash-then-sign, hash chosen explicitly); ML-DSA and SLH-DSA sign through pkeyutl instead, hashing internally. The Studio's own Workbench already branches on this — this lesson shows why.
learning_objective: Execute and contrast classical dgst and post-quantum pkeyutl signing workflows to understand hash selection and signature size differences.

title: Symmetric crypto & the myth of "PQC breaks everything"
summary: AES and SHA-256/SHA3 are NOT what post-quantum migration is about. Grover's algorithm only halves their effective security — a bigger key fixes it. Shor's algorithm breaks RSA/ECC/DH outright, which is why THOSE need new algorithms, not bigger keys.
learning_objective: Distinguish symmetric from asymmetric crypto quantum risks and explain why AES-256 requires only key doubling, not replacement.
reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 (content review vs openssl docs + bundled 3.6.3 binary)

title: Agreement & derivation
summary: ECDH lets two parties who've never met agree on a shared secret over a public channel. HKDF then turns that raw shared secret into a well-formed key.
learning_objective: Derive a shared secret using ECDH and transform it into a usable key with HKDF.

title: The Cryptoki model — slots, tokens, sessions, login
summary: Every PKCS#11 call happens through a session, opened against a token, that lives in a slot. This walkthrough boots the real engine and shows what each layer actually is — then deliberately breaks one to show what an honest failure looks like.
learning_objective: Distinguish PKCS#11 slots, tokens, and sessions to correctly handle authentication and interpret error codes.

title: Digests & randomness
summary: Two stateless building blocks used everywhere else in this curriculum: hashing and true randomness.
learning_objective: Compute SHA-256 digests and generate cryptographically strong random bytes using the hardware security token.

title: Key wrap & the extraction question
summary: Moving a key off a token requires wrapping it under another key — and PKCS#11 refuses to wrap a key that was never marked extractable, no exceptions.
learning_objective: Wrap and unwrap extractable keys while verifying that PKCS#11 blocks wrapping non-extractable keys.

title: Mechanism discovery
summary: A token doesn't support every algorithm — it advertises exactly which mechanisms it implements, and C_GetMechanismInfo is how you check before you commit to one.
learning_objective: Query token capabilities using C_GetMechanismList and C_GetMechanismInfo to verify supported mechanisms before cryptographic operations.

title: Objects & attributes
summary: Every key on a token is an object described by attributes. Two of those attributes — CKA_SENSITIVE and CKA_EXTRACTABLE — decide whether its value can ever be read back, and PKCS#11 enforces that decision permanently.
learning_objective: Generate non-extractable keys and verify that PKCS#11 permanently prevents reading their raw values.

title: Asymmetric sign & verify
summary: The private key signs, the public key verifies — and verification is a real cryptographic check, not a formality.
learning_objective: Generate RSA key pairs, sign messages, and verify signatures while correctly handling corrupted signature rejection.

title: Symmetric encryption
summary: AES-GCM is authenticated encryption — it detects tampering, not just decrypts. This walkthrough encrypts, decrypts successfully, then tampers the ciphertext and watches decryption honestly refuse it.
learning_objective: Encrypt and decrypt messages using AES-GCM, then detect tampering by observing decryption failure when ciphertext is modified.

title: Authenticated wrap
summary: C_WrapKeyAuthenticated is one of the 12 new v3.2 functions — AEAD-wrapped key export with a real IV and integrity tag, alongside the classic AES-KW wrap from lesson A7.
learning_objective: Perform authenticated key wrapping and unwrapping using AES-GCM to detect tampering in exported key material.

title: Hash-based signatures
summary: SLH-DSA has no classical predecessor to compare against — its whole point is resting on nothing but hash-function security, the most conservative assumption available.
learning_objective: Generate, sign, verify, and corrupt SLH-DSA signatures to demonstrate hash-based security and honest refusal.

title: Hedged signatures
summary: v3.2 makes randomized vs. deterministic signing an explicit, per-call choice — this walkthrough signs the same message twice each way and shows the real difference in the output bytes.
learning_objective: Configure hedging preferences to produce randomized or deterministic signatures for specific security and compliance requirements.

title: Inspecting policy and validation state
summary: Pinning a key (lesson B7) is only half the story — v3.2 also lets you read that policy BACK, so tooling can audit what's actually enforced without guessing.
learning_objective: Read and decode CKA_ALLOWED_MECHANISMS policy attributes from keys to audit enforced mechanism restrictions.

title: The KEM API
summary: C_EncapsulateKey/C_DecapsulateKey are a genuinely new call SHAPE, not just a new algorithm — no classical PKCS#11 call works this way.
learning_objective: Execute asymmetric KEM encapsulation and decapsulation to establish a shared secret using ML-KEM-768.

title: Migration capstone
summary: Put it together: inventory what is on the token, provision a PQC successor alongside a classical key, and retire the old key for real — not just mark it unused.
learning_objective: Execute a full cryptographic migration by provisioning a PQC successor, retiring the legacy key, and verifying its destruction.

title: Policy pinning
summary: CKA_ALLOWED_MECHANISMS pins a key to an explicit allow-list at creation time — the token enforces it on every later call, independent of what it otherwise supports.
learning_objective: Enforce per-key mechanism allow-lists using CKA_ALLOWED_MECHANISMS to restrict cryptographic operations at the token level.

title: Signing goes lattice
summary: RSA-3072 and ML-DSA-65 both sign and verify. Only the sizes tell you which one just quietly stopped being safe against a quantum adversary.
learning_objective: Compare RSA-3072 and ML-DSA-65 signature sizes to quantify the storage and network overhead of post-quantum migration.

title: Trust & wrapping policy
summary: CKA_WRAP_WITH_TRUSTED pins a key so only a CKA_TRUSTED wrapping key may ever wrap it out — and CKA_TRUSTED itself is the one attribute you can never set yourself, not even as the token administrator, once a key already exists.
learning_objective: Enforce key wrapping policies by generating trusted keys via SO import and verifying immutable trust attributes.

title: What's new in v3.2
summary: PKCS#11 v3.2 adds 12 new functions and a self-describing Profiles mechanism — a token can now tell you what it conforms to without vendor documentation.
learning_objective: Discover token conformance profiles and query session validation flags using PKCS#11 v3.2 APIs.

title: Attestation — the point of a TPM, in both eras (capstone)
summary: Quote platform state with a classical restricted RSA AK, then with ML-DSA — reusing everything the track taught: restricted keys, pinned schemes, PCRs, signatures, and ticket semantics.
learning_objective: Generate and compare TPM attestation quotes using classical RSA and post-quantum ML-DSA keys to evaluate signature size impacts.

title: Boot & discover — one chip, two cryptographic eras
summary: The TPM booted when this page loaded. These steps interrogate the live chip: self-test, then the algorithm table — where RSA (0x0001) and ML-KEM (0x00A0) sit side by side — and finally a deliberate rule-break to see what an honest TPM refusal looks like.
learning_objective: Query a live TPM to verify coexistence of classical and post-quantum algorithms and observe honest state-machine refusals.

title: Create primary keys — same trust model, new math
summary: Create an RSA-2048 key and an ML-KEM-768 key in the live TPM and read back what each actually produced. The hierarchy seeds, deterministic derivation, and non-exportability are identical — the public key grows from 256 bytes to 1184.
learning_objective: Create RSA-2048 and ML-KEM-768 primary keys in a TPM and compare their public key sizes and derivation methods.

title: An honest TPM — detect fake crypto and spec drift yourself
summary: A 2026 audit of this very playground found silent-placeholder risks and a compliance suite that could report a false 100%. This lesson turns those checks into things YOU run: placeholder detection, bridge status, and a live spec-vs-engine drift check.
learning_objective: Detect fake crypto placeholders and verify spec drift by running manual bridge status and signature checks.

title: Key establishment — transport vs encapsulation, loud vs silent failure
summary: Run classical RSA-OAEP key transport and ML-KEM encapsulation back to back — then corrupt a ciphertext in each system and watch them fail in OPPOSITE ways. OAEP refuses loudly; ML-KEM “succeeds” with a useless secret (implicit rejection).
learning_objective: Contrast RSA-OAEP and ML-KEM key establishment by observing their distinct loud versus silent failure modes when processing corrupted ciphertexts.

title: Sign & verify — new commands, not just new algorithms
summary: Sign with RSA through the classic TPM2_Sign, then with ML-DSA through the NEW TPM2_SignDigest — and notice V1.85 gave PQC signing its own command surface, its own signature layout, and its own verified-ticket type.
learning_objective: Execute TPM2_SignDigest and TPM2_VerifyDigestSignature to sign and verify ML-DSA signatures using the new V1.85 command surface.

title: Streaming — why pure ML-DSA must see the message
summary: Classical TPMs hash-then-sign: stream chunks into a hash sequence, sign the 32-byte digest. Pure ML-DSA signs the MESSAGE — hashing first changes the security claim — so V1.85 streams chunks into the signing operation itself. Run both flows.
learning_objective: Execute TPM streaming commands to sign and verify messages using ML-DSA, distinguishing message-level verification from classical hash-then-sign flows.

title: Factory identity — V2.7 PQC EKs and their certificates
summary: This TPM was provisioned at “manufacture” (page load) with six V2.7 PQC Endorsement Keys and X.509 certificates in well-known NV slots. Find them with live queries — persistent handles first, then the DER certificate bytes themselves.
learning_objective: Enumerate persistent handles and read V2.7 PQC EK certificates from NV slots using TPM2 commands.
